title: Mutt Carey and Buddy Petit inventing tunes on the bandstand
summary: Ridgley recalls Mutt Carey thinking up short tunes on the stand and naming them, and says Buddy Petit was good at this too.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: And then, Mutt Carey could sit on the bandstand and the Blackwood playing four hours. He could sit there and think of something, and before we leave there, he would play. You know, just get things together. He'd always come with something and he'd name it, just to give us some more funny name or something like that. And the people used to like it.
You mean he would think up a new tune and write on the bandstand?
Well, I think if he'd just been there, it wouldn't be much, you see.
Oh, I see. It wouldn't be much.

Maybe a repeat of, you see, about eight bars or something like that repeated, and then you'd add something else to it, and some other fella was in there, they'd clear on that there, he'd catch a little show, you see. I see. And everybody think if a trombone player was active, he could see something in there, too, you see.
And Mutt Carey was very good for that, and Buddy Petit.
